mcat_description.short: Prefabricated metal buildings are factory-engineered steel structures — comprising primary frames, secondary members, roof/wall cladding panels, and accessories — transported to site and bolted together for rapid erection. They are sold as complete building systems, typically custom-designed to buyer specifications for span, height, load, and end-use.
mcat_description.long: Prefabricated metal buildings, commercially known as Pre-Engineered Buildings (PEBs) in India, are structural steel systems where all components — tapered I-section primary frames, purlins, girts, bracing, and metal/sandwich panel cladding — are designed using CAD software, fabricated in a factory to precise tolerances, and assembled on-site using bolted connections. They are governed by IS:800-2007 (General Construction in Steel), IS:1893 (seismic design), and IS:875 (wind and live loads) under the Bureau of Indian Standards framework. The dominant commercial application in India is industrial and logistics infrastructure: warehouses, manufacturing sheds, cold storage facilities, aircraft hangars, and commercial complexes where large column-free spans and fast construction timelines are critical. Buyers procure these as turnkey project solutions — design, fabrication, supply, and erection — from specialist PEB manufacturers or as supply-only packages for contractor-erected projects.

market_context: In India, 'Prefabricated Metal Building' is commercially synonymous with Pre-Engineered Building (PEB) — a factory-designed and fabricated structural steel system assembled on-site. The Indian PEB market is a growing segment driven by rapid industrialisation, logistics infrastructure expansion, and government infrastructure programmes. Steel is the dominant material, with aluminium gaining share for lightweight and corrosion-resistant applications. The manufacturing sector is the largest end-user, followed by logistics and warehousing driven by e-commerce growth. Key Indian manufacturers include Interarch Building Products (pioneer since 1984), Everest Industries, Jindal Buildsys, Pennar Industries, and Zamil Steel (India operations); global players Kirby Building Systems and BlueScope Steel also operate in India. The applicable Indian standards are IS:800-2007 (General Construction in Steel — Code of Practice, BIS), IS:1893 (seismic design criteria), and IS:875 (wind and live loads). Buyers typically procure as turnkey solutions (design + fabrication + erection) or supply-only packages. The market distinguishes between heavy industrial PEBs (large clear-span warehouses, factories) and lighter modular/relocatable structures; both fall within this MCAT as sibling MCATs have already carved out portable cabins, toilets, and greenhouses. Certifications buyers look for include IS:800 compliance, ISO 9001:2015, and seismic zone compliance.
